pipelines.summary: Successfully created complete class-range backend infrastructure. ClassRangeService iterates all ships of requested type (transport/mining/auxiliary/carrier), applies PhysicsCalculator with real ShipDef data from WP-001, computes min/max/median for massRatio, dragChange, inertiaChange, and (when engine selected) topSpeed and acceleration. Ships with zero cargo are safely skipped. Engine-dependent metrics use formula: topSpeed = (thrustForward * engineCount * 1000) / dragForward. Worst-case and best-case ships identified by mass ratio. All 9 acceptance criteria met. Performance target <100ms achievable (simple iteration + math operations). All DTOs use readonly properties. No new dependencies added. Autoloader regenerated, no syntax errors.

comments.note: ClassRangeService.calculateShipMetrics() returns null for ships that fail calculations or have zero cargo. This is clean error handling — failed ships don't break the entire class-range calculation.

ClassRangeService.calculateShipMetrics() is quite long (~100 lines) and handles multiple concerns (ship data loading, physics calculation, metric extraction). Consider extracting sub-methods like loadShipPhysicsData(), calculateEngineDependentMetrics(), buildMetricsArray() for better readability and testability.

ClassRangeService uses median calculation with sort() — this is O(n log n). For large ship counts (>1000), consider optimizing with quickselect algorithm (O(n) average case). Current ship counts are ~80 per type, so this is not a concern yet.
All DTOs correctly use readonly modifier on all properties. Consistent with WP-001 implementation and constraints.md requirements.

ClassRangeService has duplicate calculatePercentChange(), calculateAverageDragChange(), and calculateAverageInertiaChange() methods that also exist in PhysicsService. Consider extracting to a shared PhysicsCalculationHelper trait or utility class to follow DRY principle.

ClassRangeEndpoint constructor creates dependencies (new ShipDataService()). This works but makes testing harder. Consider dependency injection via constructor parameter for better testability. Not critical for this iteration.

pipelines.summary: WP-002 PASSED QA validation. All 9 acceptance criteria met. Backend compiles successfully, class-range service correctly iterates ships, handles edge cases (zero cargo), and provides min/max/median aggregation. No new dependencies added. Ready for code review.

comments.description: Excellent error handling for ships with zero cargo. Returns null from calculateShipMetrics() which is then filtered out, preventing division-by-zero crashes. Clean fail-fast pattern.
All properties marked readonly - excellent immutability enforcement. Default values in fromArray() prevent null reference errors (e.g., shipType defaults to 'transport').
Clean, focused DTO with min/max/median clearly typed as float. Unit and label as strings enable frontend formatting without hardcoded assumptions.

GOLD NUGGET: Duplicate helper methods (calculatePercentChange, calculateAverageDragChange, calculateAverageInertiaChange) also exist in PhysicsService. Extract to shared PhysicsCalculationHelper trait or utility class to follow DRY principle.
Median calculation uses array_sum() + sort() approach. This is O(n log n) but perfectly acceptable for current scale (~80 ships per type). Clean implementation with proper odd/even handling.
Proper error handling with try-catch wrapping service call. Returns appropriate HTTP 500 status on errors. fromArray() parsing is clean.
Endpoint creates dependencies inline (new ShipDataService()). Consider constructor injection for better testability. Not critical for current implementation.
Route registration follows existing pattern. POST /api/calculate/class-range is RESTful and consistent with existing /api/calculate/physics endpoint.
Input validation via typed DTO properties. No code execution risks. No SQL injection (no database). fromArray() properly casts types. Division-by-zero handled gracefully.
Service iterates ~80 ships per type, performs physics calculations for each. Estimated time <100ms is realistic. No N+1 queries. Efficient median calculation for current scale.

gold_nuggets: Extract duplicate calculation helpers (calculatePercentChange, etc.) from ClassRangeService and PhysicsService into shared PhysicsCalculationHelper trait/class
Consider constructor dependency injection for ClassRangeEndpoint to improve testability
